results.question: Which S&P 500 fund you cover has the lowest annual cost once you include any swap fee?
results.answer:

Without the swap fee, Invesco's 0.05% would be lower than iShares' 0.07%. The swap fee reverses that, so the iShares fund is cheaper overall by 0.05 percentage points a year.

The factsheets are dated 30 September 2026. The KIDs show the same ranking on a different basis: iShares' KID lists management and operating costs of 0.07% [IE00B5BMR087 KID p.3], and Invesco's lists 0.05% [IE00B3YCGJ38 KID p.2], with no swap fee line in the KID.
results.judge_reasoning: Expected result: IE00B5BMR087 (iShares) with the lowest total cost, 0.07. The answer names iShares as lowest, with TER 0.07% and no swap fee, total 0.07%. It names the swap fee explicitly, giving Invesco 0.05% + 0.07% = 0.12%. The answer is substantive, not a refusal. The closing KID remark is labelled as a different basis and does not change the factsheet-based conclusion, though its claim of 'the same ranking' is inconsistent with its own KID figures (0.05 vs 0.07), a minor wording error.

results.question: Do VWRL and VWCE have the same TER?
results.answer:
Yes. Both have an Ongoing Charges Figure of 0.14% as of 30 September 2026 [IE00B3RBWM25 factsheet p.1; IE00BK5BQT80 factsheet p.1].

VWRL is the USD Distributing share class (IE00B3RBWM25), and VWCE is the USD Accumulating share class (IE00BK5BQT80). They are share classes of the same Vanguard FTSE All-World UCITS ETF and track the same index. The difference is that VWRL pays quarterly distributions, while VWCE's income is accumulated [IE00B3RBWM25 factsheet p.1; IE00BK5BQT80 factsheet p.1].

It identifies the correct ISINs and share classes (IE00B3RBWM25 Distributing, IE00BK5BQT80 Accumulating). The additional detail about quarterly distributions and index tracking is extra correct detail, not a contradiction. The answer commits to the expected result and is substantive, so it passes.
